subject: history
title: Stalin, the Great Patriotic War and Khrushchev
welcome_lead: From Stalin's terror to the de-Stalinisation of the Khrushchev era.
meta_desc: AQA A-Level adventure on Stalin's USSR, the Great Patriotic War 1941-45, and Khrushchev's de-Stalinisation through 1964.
final_note: You can assess continuity and change across the Stalinist and Khrushchev eras.

concepts.def: Centrally directed industrial plans from October 1928 prioritising heavy industry; First Plan 1928-32.
1929-33 forced amalgamation of peasant farms into kolkhozes and sovkhozes, accompanied by 'dekulakisation' and the Ukrainian famine (Holodomor) of 1932-33.
Mass purges including the Moscow Show Trials, the Yezhovshchina, and the Order 00447 operation; up to ~700,000 executed.
Soviet term for the 1941-45 conflict beginning with Operation Barbarossa on 22 June 1941; approximately 27 million Soviet dead.
Khrushchev's address to the Twentieth Party Congress on 25 February 1956 denouncing Stalin's cult of personality.
Khrushchev's 1954 programme to cultivate Kazakh and Siberian steppe; initially successful, later dogged by soil exhaustion.

walkthroughs.body_html: Stalin defeated the Left (Trotsky expelled 1927) then the Right (Bukharin 1929). The First Five-Year Plan (1928-32) and collectivisation transformed the economy: pig iron output rose four-fold by 1937, but famine in 1932-33 killed millions. The Kirov murder (1 December 1934) triggered the Great Terror; the Yezhovshchina culminated in 1937-38 with mass executions and Gulag expansion.

The Nazi-Soviet Pact (August 1939) bought time but Operation Barbarossa (22 June 1941) caught the Red Army unprepared. Defensive victories at Moscow (December 1941), Stalingrad (November 1942-February 1943) and Kursk (July 1943) turned the tide. The Red Army reached Berlin on 2 May 1945. Wartime mobilisation centralised power; victory legitimised the regime.

After Stalin's death (5 March 1953), Beria was executed; Khrushchev emerged dominant by 1955. The Secret Speech (February 1956) opened the 'Thaw'. The Hungarian Rising (October-November 1956) was crushed. Sputnik (October 1957) and Gagarin (April 1961) symbolised technological prestige. Failures over Cuba (October 1962), agriculture and the 'harebrained scheming' charge led the Politburo to depose Khrushchev on 14 October 1964.
